reply_text:
The key list has never had a `Dionysus` entry. Maybe the June pushes were made on the box itself, so I'm looking for a clone there.`Dionysus` has never been in git's key list by that name. Your June pushes did come from a key that was on the list, though, and I think I removed it by mistake on 14 September.

On the 14th I pruned git's key list down to the five named laptops. One of the keys I removed has **no machine name attached**:

```
256 SHA256:puXHaLLa9BTHB0GnO9xzRZdED+m2GG7D6bSQ1vbT97A  (ED25519, no comment)
```

It's the only modern-style key that was on the list. Since all five named laptops are dead, it's almost certainly the key Dionysus pushed with in June. That means git over SSH has probably been broken for you since the prune on the 14th, not since tonight's move. The other keys removed then were `zanzi@tangle`, `pair@metameso.org` and `mieza@DESKTOP-39BD3CH`.

To confirm, run this on Dionysus:

```
ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

If it prints `SHA256:puXHaLLa9BTHB0GnO9xzRZdED+m2GG7D6bSQ1vbT97A`, tell me and I'll put that key back. The pre-prune list is saved on the box, so it's a one-line restore. Then `git ls-remote git@metameso.org:joe-homepage.git` from Dionysus should show `d04ee5c`, and a trivial push should update `/~joe/`.

If the fingerprint is different, or you can't get to Dionysus right now, the alternative is to add Zone's key to the list. Then you can clone and push from Zone, at the cost of a 1.3 GB download for the first clone.

I've also noticed that I don't know which laptops are dead. Do you want me to remove the five dead laptops' keys from git and from joe's login on the box?
